## Natural history notes

A small longhorn beetle characterized by a slender, dark brown to nearly black body, long antennae, and narrow cylindrical form typical of twig- and branch-boring cerambycids. In Florida, Heterachthes ebenus is most likely found in wooded or semi-wooded habitats such as hammocks, forest edges, parks, yards, and shrubby areas where suitable dead or weakened host wood occurs. Adults may come to lights or rest on woody vegetation, while the larvae bore in dead or dying branches; host records include flowering dogwood in the southeastern United States, so it helps recycle woody material and supports woodpeckers, parasitoid wasps, and other forest predators.
